$comment: The Contract T tool registry, the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for tools. The bridge loads this at startup; llm receive it as their tool list; the executor refuses calls not defined here. tier: 1=read-only, 2=reversible (earcon announce), 3=destructive (spoken confirmation required). Growth rule: a new tool needs no approval, only a record of when it was built and whether it has been invoked in real use without misfiring.
$comment_connector: Every tool also declares the CONSENT card it sits under. Tier and connector are orthogonal gates — the tier says whether the app MAY (danger, the designer's judgement), the connector says whether the user WANTS it to (consent, theirs). Both must pass or the tool is not offered and is refused if called. The id is matched to a `connector` setting in schemas/settings.json, which holds the label, the default and what it reaches; a new tool joins an existing card by naming it here, with no UI work.
$comment_label: `label` is the tool said in a sentence a person would use, for the connector card to list — consent to a card has to be consent to something specific, and `description` is written for the model, not for a reader. It belongs here rather than in the window because the registry is the tool's own truth; nothing in code or QML restates it.

tools.name: system_status
tools.label: Read the time, battery and active window
tools.description: Report the current local date and time WITH its UTC offset (use the offset to work out the time in other time zones yourself), plus battery (if a laptop), volume level, active window title, and media playback state.

tools.name: read_clipboard
tools.label: Read what you last copied
tools.description: Return the current text contents of the clipboard (truncated to 2000 chars).

tools.name: find_document
tools.label: Find a file by name or content
tools.description: Find files on this PC by what they CONTAIN or are named, using the Windows Search index — use this for 'find the document about X', 'the letter I wrote last month', and similar. Returns up to 8 matches (name, date modified, full path), best match first. Searches only what Windows has already indexed; nothing leaves the machine.

query.description: the distinguishing words to look for in file contents and names — plain terms only, no operators or punctuation

kind.description: optional: restrict to one kind of item

since.description: optional: only items modified on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: search_email
tools.label: Search your inbox for a message
tools.description: Search the mail in the desktop Outlook inbox and return matching HEADERS only — sender, date received, subject — up to 8, newest first. Use for 'the email from Sarah about the lease', 'what did X send me last week'. Every parameter is optional and they are combined with AND; give only the ones the request actually implies. Bodies are searched but never returned, and nothing is opened, replied to or sent.

sender.description: optional: part of the sender's name or email address

subject.description: optional: words appearing in the subject line

query.description: optional: free text — each word must appear in the subject or the body

since.description: optional: only mail received on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD

before.description: optional: only mail received before this date, as YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: open_app
tools.label: Open an app
tools.description: Launch an application by the name a person would say for it (e.g. 'spotify', 'word', 'notepad'). Resolved against the apps this PC actually has; if the name matches nothing, the closest installed names come back so you can offer them instead of guessing again.

app.description: what the app is called, in plain words — never a path or a command line

tools.name: focus_window
tools.label: Bring a window to the front
tools.description: Bring an already-open window to the front. Matches against the titles of the windows open right now; if none matches, the closest open titles come back. Use this to switch to something running — use open_app to start something that is not.

title_query.description: a distinctive word or two from the window's title, or the app's name

tools.name: media_control
tools.label: Press the media and volume keys
tools.description: Send a media key: play/pause, next, previous, volume_up, volume_down, mute_toggle.

tools.name: set_timer
tools.label: Set a timer
tools.description: Set a named countdown timer; the bridge plays the 'timer' earcon and speaks the name when it fires.
